page: Amazon Web Services c6in.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8375C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz and includes 54 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance in single-core operations, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.09 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1518.0. However, multi-core and memory-bound workloads show relative limitations, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 3252.0 and a passmark memory score categorized as poor. The instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 27.68 GB/sec and static web serving throughput at 6.49 GB/sec, but falls into weaker categories for database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression.

This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated compute resources and high-frequency single-core execution without demanding massive memory footprints or local storage. It is suitable for web serving, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight network-optimized tasks.
